Subject: Pilot opt-out flow and prompt/response ownership — Nexus Health pilot DPA

Hi Liam,

Thanks again for taking the call this morning. Attached is the draft DPA with the pilot carveouts we discussed (Nexus_pilot_DPA_draft.pdf). To keep the pilot moving, could you confirm the three items below so we can turn around an ops/evidence pack quickly?

1) No-model-learning scope — our proposed wording: Redwood will not use customer-provided inputs or associated outputs to update model weights or otherwise improve model parameters. This allows ephemeral caching for latency but not weight updates. Is that acceptable for Nexus's pilot?

2) Prompt & response ownership — Nexus asked for clarity on whether you retain ownership of prompts and generated responses. We typically grant customers ownership of their prompts and a license to use generated outputs; if you need an exclusive assignment for results in the pilot, please specify.

3) Residency / deletion SLA — for pilot data we can offer: a) onshore routing for EU/US as needed, b) deletion on request within 30 days for pilot artifacts, and c) optional SFTP export for evidence. Would you like onshore KMS as part of the pilot?

Next steps I propose: if the three bullets look good, Marissa will prepare an operational evidence pack (how we enforce no-learning, subprocessor list, audit logs) and Kimberly can confirm subprocessor gating for the pilot.

I've cc'd Marissa. Attachment: Nexus_pilot_DPA_draft.pdf (draft for review).

Thanks,

--
David Kim

Thanks David — appreciate the quick turnaround and the call. A few clarifying questions before we loop legal: 

- No-model-learning: The language looks promising. Can you confirm whether any telemetry or aggregated telemetry derived from pilot requests (latency measurements, anonymized usage patterns) could be used to fine-tune service behavior? Nexus needs a clear distinction between telemetry for platform ops vs. any training use.

- Prompt/response ownership: Nexus' legal asks for an explicit statement that Nexus "retains all rights, title and interest in and to prompts and customer-provided data" and that output (responses) are assigned to Nexus for the pilot duration; after pilot, we can revisit license terms. Is Redwood able to sign off on assignment for pilot outputs (limited to this engagement)?

- Evidence: procurement has asked for what you call an "evidence pack" — can you enumerate what that'll include (logs, attestation, subprocessor list, proof of deletion procedure)? They prefer an exportable zip.

I've attached the procurement questionnaire procurement_questionnaire.xlsx with our usual info requests. I've cc'd procurement.

Hi Liam (and team),

Quick clarifications from legal/ops perspective — thanks for the questionnaire, we'll use that to scope deliverables. High level answers below; I'll assemble the formal evidence pack as a PDF/zip once we agree a path.

- Telemetry vs training: Redwood's defined practice is that platform telemetry (e.g., latency, error rates, anonymized usage metrics) is used solely for platform reliability and capacity planning and is not fed back into model training or parameter updates. The "no-model-learning" clause in the draft explicitly excludes telemetry used strictly for ops. We can add an explicit sentence: "Telemetry used for system performance, reliability, or aggregate usage analytics will not be used to update model weights or train models."

- Prompt & response ownership: For pilot customers we can: a) confirm customer retains ownership of prompts/customer-provided data; and b) grant an assignment/ownership of generated outputs for the pilot term (we can put a limited assignment clause into the pilot exhibit). Post-pilot, outputs revert to our standard license unless otherwise negotiated. Please confirm that a time-limited assignment (pilot start/end dates) works for Nexus.

- Evidence pack contents (what we'll deliver):
  * Operational description of the no-learning technical guardrail (how we prevent weight updates)
  * Subprocessor inventory for the pilot (with gating controls)
  * Sample audit logs showing request traces and deletion flow (sanitized)
  * Proof-of-deletion procedure and template deletion attestations
  * Optional onshore KMS configuration notes (if you opt for onshore key management)

Attachments: no_learn_ops_and_evidence.pdf (high-level ops description + checklist).

Kimberly, can you confirm whether the subprocessor gating we discussed (explicit approval for any new subprocessor touching pilot data) is acceptable and whether we should include a 48-hour notification SLA in the pilot exhibit?

Liam — if you confirm pilots' need for assignment for outputs (and whether you want onshore KMS), we'll draft the pilot exhibit and a short DocuSign-ready signature page.

Thanks,
Marissa

--
Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Security, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Pilot opt-out flow and prompt/response ownership — Nexus Health pilot DPA

Thanks Marissa — this is helpful. A few follow-ups from procurement and legal (Elaine copied):

- Assignment timing: Nexus can accept a limited assignment of outputs for pilot duration (good). We need explicit start/end dates and a clause that post-pilot the assignment expires and usage rights revert per Redwood standard terms.

- Subprocessor gating: procurement wants a 72-hour notice for any subprocessor change (rather than 48). Is Redwood able to do 72 hours for the pilot?

- Evidence pack delivery: procurement requests the evidence pack as a downloadable ZIP and a one-hour walkthrough with ops. Can you confirm delivery by next Wednesday 11 June?

- Deletion SLA: Nexus needs deletion within 14 days for pilot artifacts, not 30, and a signed deletion attestation after purge. Is 14 days feasible?

I've attached procurement_questionnaire.xlsx with some additional requests.
